topics.title: Laboratory B.1 — Descriptor identity and open-description state
topics.summary: The descriptor lab creates and unlinks its own temporary file, marks the original descriptor close-on-exec, and duplicates it. The two descriptor numbers differ, their close-on-exec flags differ under the chosen dup operation, and their reads advance the same open-file offset. It then closes one owner and continues through the other. This distinguishes descriptor-local state from state shared through an open file description. (OPEN, POSIXCLOSE)

blocks.text: Reason through the result. Closing the first descriptor does not close the duplicate. Moving the duplicate transfers its one ownership obligation. The test’s self-move goes through the owner’s public move-assignment contract. It does not re-adopt a borrowed integer through reset; that operation requires a genuinely new ownership value or the invalid sentinel.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix B — Complete Systems Laboratories and Shared Support
topics.title: Laboratory B.2 — Framing under every bounded three-chunk split
topics.summary: The frame lab constructs deterministic payloads of lengths zero through sixty-four and feeds their wire encodings at every pair of chunk boundaries. Some chunks are empty, some split the header, and others split the payload. Every history must yield the same exact byte string. A manually specified wire value with byte 255 provides an independent check rather than relying on round-trip consistency alone.

blocks.text: The shared FrameDecoder implementation is listed in Appendix C. Its returned consumed count stops at the end of one frame, allowing the caller to retain subsequent bytes for another decoder. Failed decoders cannot be reused as though a framing error had not happened. The separate registered codec cases test oversized headers, maximum-length payloads, and truncated input.

topics.title: Laboratory B.3 — Accepted-item conservation and startup cleanup
topics.summary: Two producers submit disjoint ID ranges through a capacity-three blocking queue, while three consumers collect into separate vectors. After joining, the test combines and sorts the observed IDs. It expects exactly the accepted set with no duplicates or omissions. It does not require an arbitrary total order among concurrent producers.

blocks.text: The lab also injects failure after a consumer starts but before its partner is launched. A close-before-join guard changes the waiting predicate during unwinding. The already-started consumer exits while its queue remains alive. This deterministic seam tests the lifecycle policy without exhausting actual operating-system thread resources.

blocks.text: Reason through the result. Each consumer owns its output vector, and the supervisor reads them only after joining. Shared queue state is protected internally. The guard’s declaration order ensures it closes before worker-vector destruction joins. Moving the guard earlier would change exceptional cleanup order and could reintroduce the hang the test is designed to prevent.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix B — Complete Systems Laboratories and Shared Support
topics.title: Laboratory B.4 — A reusable single-producer/single-consumer handoff
topics.summary: The publication lab adds the reverse ownership handoff missing from a reusable Boolean-ready sketch. State zero grants the producer access to the payload; state one grants it to the consumer; state two closes the channel. Release/acquire operations transfer permission in both directions. Compare-exchange prevents either participant from overwriting the terminal closed state during a concurrent stop.

blocks.text: This is exactly one producer and one consumer with one integer slot. It is not a multi-producer queue, not a lock-free reclamation scheme, and not a guarantee that the standard library’s atomic waiting implementation never uses operating-system blocking. A close can abandon an in-flight value; the lab’s ordinary path instead transfers all five thousand values before closure.

topics.title: Shared assertion helper
topics.summary: The checks throw an exception with source location when a condition fails. They are not compiled out by NDEBUG, which is why Release fixture execution remains meaningful. Worker functions must not let these exceptions escape a thread entry point; they either avoid checks inside the worker or catch and transfer failures to the supervisor.

topics.title: Shared blocking queue used by Chapters 18 and 21
topics.summary: This queue is element-count bounded and drains accepted items after closure. Its by-value push can consume a caller argument before returning false. The deque may allocate during insertion, and the item type must be nothrow move-constructible. Keep these properties distinct from the extended server’s nonblocking admission queue in Appendix C.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix B — Complete Systems Laboratories and Shared Support
topics.title: Shared elementary Linux adapter
topics.summary: The compact chapter examples use the following adapter for descriptor ownership, exact byte transfers, bounded framing, and loopback endpoints. Its socket timeouts and readiness waits are useful for controlled finite examples. They do not form one absolute deadline across every header, body, response, and admission stage. The extended adapter in Appendix C supplies that stronger operation-level mechanism separately.
